title: Graph construction of the global operator
statement:
Let $(h,v)$ be a graph correspondence with $h$ proper. The global
operator $T_c(v)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is the composite

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,Lh^*K)
\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,v)}R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where the first arrow is induced by the unit
$K\to Rh_*Lh^*K$ and the canonical identification
$Rh_*\simeq Rh_!$. It is functorial in $(K,v)$, additive in
distinguished triangles, and compatible with composition of proper
endomorphisms.

proof.text:
Put $H=R\Gamma_c(X,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{X!}$, using the coefficient conventions already included in [def-trf-global-operator]. For the graph of [def-trf-graph-correspondence], $C=X$, $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $c_2=h$, and $u=v:Lh^*K\to K$. In the defining composite of [def-trf-global-operator], the last composition identification and the exceptional counit for $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ cancel: the identity adjunction has identity counit by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and the identity composition comparison is the identity by [prop-functor-package], clause (3). Write $\rho_h:Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_!$ for the inverse of the proper comparison, and $\alpha_{a,h}:Ra_{X!}Rh_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(a_Xh)_!=Ra_{X!}$ for compact-support composition (followed by $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ when applied to $H$). The latter equality uses that $h$ is a $k$-endomorphism. Then the remaining composite is exactly
$$q_{h,K}=\alpha_{a,h,Lh^*K}\circ H(\rho_{h,Lh^*K})\circ H(\eta_{h,K}):H(K)\longrightarrow H(Lh^*K),\qquad T_{h,v}=H(v)\circ q_{h,K}.$$
Here $\eta_h$ is the ordinary pullback/direct-image unit, not an exceptional counit. Properness is precisely the hypothesis needed for $\rho_h$; no properness of $X/k$ is assumed.

source.place: displayed graph specialization and the sentence identifying the proper comparison and identity counit

proof.text: For fixed $h$, apply [lem-trf-global-operator-naturality] to its graph: a map $f:K\to K'$ of coefficient pairs satisfies $f\circ v=v'\circ Lh^*f$ and hence $H(f)\circ T_{h,v}=T_{h,v'}\circ H(f)$. Explicitly, naturality of the unit, proper comparison and composition comparison in Step 1 gives $q_{h,K'}\circ H(f)=H(Lh^*f)\circ q_{h,K}$; composing with $H(v')$ and substituting the pair relation gives the claimed square. The graph has identity exceptional leg, so it is admissible, and its ordinary leg is proper by hypothesis. This proves functoriality in $(K,v)$.

Let $K_1\to K_2\to K_3\to K_1[1]$ be a distinguished triangle and let $v_i:Lh^*K_i\to K_i$ be a morphism from its pulled-back triangle to itself, including the square for the connecting arrow. Specialize [lem-trf-global-operator-triangulated] to $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $c_2=h$. Its conclusion says that the three maps $T_{h,v_i}=H(v_i)q_{h,K_i}$ form an endomorphism of the compact-cohomology distinguished triangle. Thus all three squares, including the connecting square with its shift comparison, commute. This is the distinguished-triangle compatibility (the additivity clause) of the global operator. It concerns compatible coefficient triangles; it does not assert a trace identity for arbitrary triangle endomorphisms.

source.place: last sentence: additivity over distinguished triangles

proof.text:
Let $g,h:X\to X$ be proper $k$-endomorphisms. Their composite $h\circ g$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Use $L(h\circ g)^*\simeq Lg^*Lh^*$. With $f=g$ and the outer morphism $h$, clause (3) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] gives the typed identity
$$\eta_{h\circ g,K}=Rh_*(\eta_{g,Lh^*K})\circ\eta_{h,K}$$
under the ordinary composition comparisons. Apply $H$ and then the proper and compact-support comparisons of Step 1. By [prop-functor-package], clause (3), and the identity/composition coherence of [fix-prop-coherence], the comparison $H R(h\circ g)_*\simeq H R(h\circ g)_!\simeq H$ is the composite $H Rh_*Rg_*\simeq H Rh_!Rg_!\simeq H Rg_!\simeq H$. For clarity, put $b_{h,N}=\alpha_{a,h,N}\circ H(\rho_{h,N}):H(Rh_*N)\to H(N)$. Its naturality on $\eta_{g,Lh^*K}$ reads $H(\eta_g)\circ b_{h,Lh^*K}=b_{h,Rg_*Lg^*Lh^*K}\circ H(Rh_*\eta_g)$, and coherence reads $b_{h\circ g}=b_g\circ b_h Rg_*$ under the composition comparisons. Thus $q_g\circ q_h=b_g H(\eta_g)b_h H(\eta_h)=b_g b_h Rg_* H(Rh_*\eta_g)H(\eta_h)=b_{h\circ g}H(\eta_{h\circ g})$. In other words the displayed unit equation becomes
$$q_{h\circ g,K}=q_{g,Lh^*K}\circ q_{h,K}:H(K)\longrightarrow H(Lg^*Lh^*K).$$
For an identity endomorphism the same comparisons and the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give $q_{\operatorname{id},K}=\operatorname{id}_{H(K)}$. These assertions are at finite coefficient level $A=A_{E,n}$ on the constructible domains of the graph correspondence; no completed or rational pullback is substituted.

The unit sk-d-operator is a definition with no proof steps; this item is its graph specialization, not its key definition.

tool_uses.why: Its proper coincidence and coherent compact-support composition are the operation data used by sk-d-six; they identify the arrows defining the graph operator.
Clause (3) gives the ordinary composite-unit equation with the correct typing; sk-d-operator assumes the operation package but has no separate theorem spelling out this identity.
It supplies coherence of the canonical proper and composition comparisons when the two unit insertions are compared; this implements the sk-d-six package, not a replacement route.
The general correspondence triangle statement specializes to a graph and supplies the triangle clause; the operator unit has no more specialized triangle theorem.
